mainTopic: Sources for the כרת requirement in sin-offerings, and why the משנה counts fifteen women
overview: This amud asks where we learn that the sin-offerings for a mistaken sin, brought by an individual, a נשיא, the משיח or the community, apply only to sins that carry כרת when done on purpose. רבי learns it from the word "עליה," which links the communal offering to the prohibition of אחות אשה. From there, other links like "לאשמת העם," "מצות," "מעיני" and the ו of "ואם נפש" carry the rule to every case, including עבודה זרה. The רבנן use "עליה" for the צרות, so they learn the rule from "תורה אחת," which compares the whole Torah to עבודה זרה. רבי uses "תורה אחת" instead to teach that individuals and the many bring the same offering for עבודה זרה, even though their punishments differ. רב חלקיה asks why that is needed, and the גמרא gives two answers. Then לוי asks רבי why the משנה lists fifteen women and not sixteen. רבי answers that the extra case is disputed, and our chapter lists only agreed cases. The גמרא tests that rule against several cases, and a new challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Idolatry also needs a כרת-level act
steps.stepSummary: The end of a quoted משנה: even with עבודה זרה, the communal offering applies only if the act carries כרת when done on purpose and a חטאת when done by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not for idolatry either, unless it is about something that brings כרת if done on purpose and a חטאת if done by mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a משנה that sets the limits of the special offering brought when the בית דין rules in error. This line adds that the same limit applies to עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the משנה, the communal offering was limited to sins that carry כרת on purpose and חטאת by mistake. This line says עבודה זרה is no exception. Only an act of idolatry that meets that standard brings the offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Idolatry, worship of foreign gods
Doing it on purpose
Doing it by mistake
Spiritual 'cutting off,' the heavenly punishment for certain serious sins
Sin-offering brought for a mistaken sin

phrases.english: And not for idolatry either,
phrases.notes: This is the tail end of a משנה the גמרא started quoting just before this. It is talking about the offering brought when the בית דין rules wrongly.

phrases.english: except for a matter
for whose intentional violation one is liable to כרת
and for its unintentional violation a sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, אֶלָּא עַל דָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a משנה quote that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The communal offering for עבודה זרה also requires an act that carries כרת on purpose and חטאת by mistake.

steps.title: Which offering each person brings
steps.stepSummary: A second משנה lists the offerings for a mistaken כרת-level sin: a יחיד, a נשיא, a משיח and the בית דין each bring their own type, and there is a separate list for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also learned in a משנה: for any מצוה in the Torah that brings כרת if done on purpose and a חטאת if done by mistake, an ordinary person brings a female lamb or female goat, a נשיא brings a male goat, and the משיח and בית דין bring a bull. For idolatry, an ordinary person, a נשיא and a משיח all bring a female goat, while the community brings a bull and a goat: the bull as an עולה and the goat as a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another משנה. It confirms the same rule, that these offerings are only for כרת-and-חטאת sins, and it lists which animal each type of person brings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ordinary sins, the offering depends on who sinned: a lamb or goat, a male goat, or a bull. For עבודה זרה the pattern changes. All individuals, even the נשיא and משיח, bring a female goat, and the community brings two animals.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary individual
The king or ruler of the nation
The anointed כהן גדול
A bull
A female goat / a male goat
Burnt-offering, burned entirely on the altar

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up שעירה (female goat) with שעיר (male goat). The נשיא brings a male goat for ordinary sins, but a female goat for idolatry.

phrases.english: And we also learned in a mishna:
Any מצוה in the Torah
for whose intentional violation one is liable to כרת
and for its unintentional violation a sin-offering:
an individual brings a ewe or a she-goat,
a נשיא brings a male goat,
the anointed priest and the court bring a bull.
And for idolatry,
an individual, a נשיא and the anointed priest bring a she-goat,
the community brings a bull and a goat,
the bull as a burnt-offering and the goat as a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second משנה that states the same כרת-and-חטאת requirement and spells out the offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offerings for mistaken כרת-level sins are set by who sinned, and עבודה זרה has its own separate list.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the Torah source that these offerings apply only to sins with כרת and חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule just quoted. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משניות stated the rule but gave no פסוק for it. The גמרא wants to know how we know that the communal offering is limited to sins with כרת and חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule the two משניות stated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that the communal offering applies only to sins carrying כרת on purpose and חטאת by mistake.

steps.title: The word "עליה" links to the wife's sister
steps.stepSummary: רבי uses a גזירה שוה. The word "עליה" appears in the communal-offering passage and in the prohibition of אחות אשה. Since that prohibition carries כרת and חטאת, so does the communal offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: "And the sin by which they sinned becomes known." רבי says: it says "עליה" here, and it says "עליה" there. Just as there it is a matter that brings כרת on purpose and a חטאת by mistake, so too here it must be a matter that brings כרת on purpose and a חטאת by mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא in which רבי links two פסוקים through the shared word "עליה."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The "there" is the prohibition of marrying a wife's sister, which carries כרת on purpose and a חטאת by mistake. The shared word moves that standard over to the communal offering. Here רבי uses the "עליה" of אחות אשה for this גזירה שוה, while the רבנן use that word for the צרות. That is why the גמרא later asks for the רבנן's own source (step 11).

keyTerms.meaning: Learning one law from another because the same word appears in both
'On it / upon her,' the shared word that links the two passages
'There,' meaning the other passage being compared
A wife's sister, forbidden while the wife is alive

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that communal offerings apply only to כרת-and-חטאת sins comes from the word "עליה," which links them to the prohibition of אחות אשה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of the sugya. Because רבי and the רבנן read "עליה" differently, the גמרא goes on to find the רבנן's own source (steps 11-12) and then asks what רבי does with "תורה אחת" (step 17).

"And the sin by which they sinned becomes known,"

phrases.notes: "There" is the פסוק about marrying your wife's sister, ויקרא 18:18.

phrases.english: Just as there it is a matter
for whose intentional violation one is liable to כרת
and for its unintentional violation a sin-offering,
so too here it is a matter
for whose intentional violation one is liable to כרת
and for its unintentional violation a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of "עליה" from אחות אשה, which carries כרת and חטאת.

steps.title: What about the משיח?
steps.stepSummary: The rule is proven for the community. Where do we learn it for the anointed כהן גדול?
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found the source for the community. How do we know it for the משיח?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that the גזירה שוה covered only the community's offering. It now asks for a source for the משיח, setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "עליה" appears in the community's passage, not in the משיח's. So the גמרא needs a separate reason to apply the כרת-and-חטאת limit to the משיח too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We have found' (one case is proven)
The community
'From where do we know it?'

phrases.english: We have found a source for the community;
from where do we derive it for the anointed priest?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the question from step 3 to the משיח.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that the משיח's offering is also limited to sins with כרת and חטאת.

steps.title: The משיח is like the community
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק "לאשמת העם" shows that the משיח is treated like the community, so the same rule applies to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written about the משיח: "to bring guilt on the people." So the משיח is like the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק about the משיח that ties him to the people. Whatever applies to the community therefore applies to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "לאשמת העם" links the משיח's sin to the community. That link carries over the limit already learned for the community from "עליה": the משיח's offering also applies only to sins with כרת and חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To bring guilt on the people'
'Behold / so,' introducing the conclusion

steps.whatToRemember: The community learns the כרת-and-חטאת rule from "עליה" (אחות אשה), and the משיח learns it from the community through "לאשמת העם."

phrases.english: As it is written about the anointed priest:
"to bring guilt on the people,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:3

phrases.english: so the anointed priest is like the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by linking the משיח to the community.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "לאשמת העם" makes the משיח like the community, so the same כרת-and-חטאת limit applies to him.

steps.title: The individual and the נשיא are learned from the word "מצות"
steps.stepSummary: The rule that only כרת-level sins bring these offerings is extended to the individual and the נשיא through a גזירה שוה on the word "מצות".
steps.simpleTranslation: An individual and a נשיא: this is learned from "מצוות" and "מצוות".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the source for the two people still left on the list: the ordinary individual and the נשיא. It links them to the community through a shared word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "מצות" appears in the community's passage, the נשיא's passage and the individual's passage. The community was already shown to need a כרת-and-חטאת sin. The shared word passes that same requirement on to the נשיא and the individual.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes from, meaning it is learned from (a גזירה שוה)
Commandments; the word shared by all three passages
An ordinary private individual
The king or tribal leader, who brings his own kind of offering

phrases.english: A private individual and a Nasi (leader) —
it is learned from "מצוות" and "מצוות."
phrases.notes: The word shows up for the community, the נשיא and the individual: ויקרא 4:13, 22, 27.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the first list of the משנה. After the community (step 4) and the משיח (step 6), it covers the remaining two people.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה "מצות"–"מצות" carries the community's כרת requirement over to the individual and the נשיא.

steps.title: The community's offering for עבודה זרה is learned from the word "מעיני"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule for עבודה זרה and gives the source for the community from a גזירה שוה on "מעיני".
steps.simpleTranslation: And in עבודה זרה, only for something that brings כרת when done on purpose and a חטאת when done by mistake. The community in עבודה זרה learns this from "from the eyes" and "from the eyes".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second list in the משנה, the special offerings for mistaken עבודה זרה. It first gives the source for the community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "מעיני" appears in the regular community-offering passage, which needs a כרת sin. It also appears in the community's עבודה זרה passage. The shared word teaches that the עבודה זרה offering also applies only to a כרת-and-חטאת sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Idol worship
Doing it on purpose
Doing it by mistake
From the eyes (of the community); the word shared by the two passages

phrases.english: And for idol worship, not unless it is

phrases.english: for a matter where doing it on purpose brings karet
and doing it by mistake brings a sin-offering.
The community, for idol worship,
learns it from "eyes" and "from the eyes."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:13 says "מעיני הקהל" and במדבר 15:24 says "מעיני העדה".

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֶלָּא עַל דָּבָר שֶׁחַיָּיבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the regular list to the עבודה זרה list of the משנה. It begins with the community, just as the first list did.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה "מעיני"–"מעיני" links the community's עבודה זרה offering to its regular offering, which needs a כרת sin.

steps.title: The individual, נשיא and משיח in עבודה זרה are learned from "ואם נפש אחת"
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק, "ואם נפש אחת", covers the individual, the נשיא and the משיח. Its opening ו ties it to the community's פסוק before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: An individual, a נשיא and a משיח are learned from "And if one person". The individual, the נשיא and the משיח are all included in it. The letter ו adds onto the first topic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the three single people in the עבודה זרה list. It also points out the word "and" that connects their פסוק to the community's פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "נפש אחת" (one person) is broad enough to include anyone who sins alone: an individual, a נשיא or a משיח. Because the פסוק begins with "ו" (and), it continues the topic before it, the community's עבודה זרה. That sets up the comparison in the next step.

"And if one person": the פסוק about a single person's mistaken עבודה זרה
Included in the meaning of the words

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the community's source for עבודה זרה, it covers the single persons and links their פסוק to the community's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "ואם נפש אחת" includes all three. Its ו connects it to the community's passage.

steps.title: The single person's rule is learned from the community's
steps.stepSummary: Because the פסוקים are linked, the single person's עבודה זרה offering also requires a כרת-and-חטאת sin, just like the community's.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let the lower one be learned from the upper one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion. The lower פסוק (single persons) takes on the rule of the upper פסוק (the community).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The community's עבודה זרה offering was shown in step 8 to need a כרת-level sin. Since the ו joins the two passages, that same limit now applies to the individual, the נשיא and the משיח.

keyTerms.meaning: And let it be learned
The lower one: the later פסוק, about single persons
The upper one: the earlier פסוק, about the community

steps.whatToRemember: Every part of the משנה's lists has its own source. The community and the משיח come from "עליה" and "לאשמת העם". The individual and the נשיא come from "מצות". The community's עבודה זרה offering comes from "מעיני". The single persons' עבודה זרה offering comes from the ו of "ואם נפש אחת". So all of them apply only to a sin with כרת and a חטאת.

phrases.english: so let the lower one be learned from the upper one.
phrases.notes: "Lower" is the single person's פסוק and "upper" is the community's פסוק just before it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reasoning of step 9 by applying the link it set up.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The individual, נשיא and משיח bring the עבודה זרה offering only for a sin with כרת on purpose and a חטאת by mistake, the same as the community.

steps.title: Where do the Rabbis get this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the רבנן get the rule that only a כרת-level sin brings a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, where do they get this idea from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא switches from רבי to the רבנן and asks for their source. This sets up the next step, where the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי got the כרת rule from a source the רבנן use for something else, the rival wives. So the רבנן need their own source for the same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion
Idea, line of reasoning
From where do they know it?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, this idea, from where do they get it?
phrases.notes: The רבנן use the word 'עליה' for the rival wives, so they need a different source for the כרת rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing רבי's source, the גמרא asks the same question about the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The רבנן's source for the rule that a חטאת comes only for a sin that carries כרת when done on purpose.

steps.title: One law compares the whole Torah to idolatry
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'תורה אחת' links the whole Torah to עבודה זרה. So any sin that brings a חטאת must be one that carries כרת when done on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learn it from the פסוקים רבי יהושע taught his son: 'One law for the one who acts by mistake' and 'the soul that acts with a high hand.' These compare the whole Torah to עבודה זרה. Just as עבודה זרה carries כרת on purpose and a חטאת by mistake, so too any sin brings a חטאת only if it carries כרת on purpose and a חטאת by mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's source. The phrase 'תורה אחת' makes the whole Torah follow the rules of עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים are about עבודה זרה. The next פסוק says that doing it on purpose brings כרת. Because the פסוק says 'one Torah', every מצוה is compared to this case, which is a הקש, so only כרת-level sins bring a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Was compared (a הֶקֵּשׁ, a comparison the פסוק makes)
Doing it on purpose
Doing it by mistake
With a high hand, meaning boldly and on purpose
Being cut off, a heavenly punishment
Sin-offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the רבנן's main source for the כרת requirement across the whole Torah.

steps.title: What about the community in idolatry?
steps.stepSummary: The single person, the נשיא and the משיח are covered for every sin. The גמרא asks where the community's עבודה זרה is learned from.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have a source for the individual, the נשיא and the משיח, both for עבודה זרה and for other מצוות. For the community in עבודה זרה, where is the source?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up who is covered so far. It then asks about the one case still missing, the community sinning in עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תורה אחת' sits in the section about a single person, so it covers only people judged as one person. The community has its own separate section, so it needs its own source.

steps.title: The upper section learns from the lower
steps.stepSummary: The ו in 'ואם נפש' links the community's section to the individual's, so the community learns from the individual.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'And if a soul', so let the upper section, the community, learn from the lower one, the individual.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers using the extra ו, the word 'and', at the start of the individual's פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a later section learns from an earlier one. Here the ו joins the two sections, so the community's section, which comes first, takes on the rule of the individual's section, which comes after it.

keyTerms.meaning: Upper, meaning the section written earlier
Lower, meaning the section written later

steps.confusionAlert: Don't flip the direction. The earlier section, the community, is the one learning from the later section, the individual.

phrases.english: The verse says: "And if a soul,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:27

phrases.english: and let the upper learn from the lower.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13, using the same ו as step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ו links the two sections, so the community's עבודה זרה also needs a כרת-level sin.

steps.title: What about the community in other commandments?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source for the community in the rest of the מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the community in other מצוות, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: One more case is still left, the community sinning in other מצוות, and the גמרא asks for its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 covered only the community's עבודה זרה. The community's offering for other מצוות comes in a different section, ויקרא 4, which is not linked by the ו.

keyTerms.meaning: But, still
The other commandments
From where do we know?

phrases.english: But the community in other commandments, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spots the last gap after step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for the community needing a כרת-level sin in other מצוות.

steps.title: Learned from the word from the eyes
steps.stepSummary: A גזירה שוה on 'מעיני' links the community's other מצוות to its עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'from the eyes' and 'from the eyes'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the same גזירה שוה it used earlier, so the community's other מצוות follow its עבודה זרה rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מעיני' shows up in both community sections. That shared word carries the כרת rule from the community's עבודה זרה over to its other מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: A link made through the same word appearing in two places
From the eyes (of the community)
He learns it

steps.whatToRemember: For the רבנן, every case now needs a כרת-level sin. The single person comes from 'תורה אחת', the community's עבודה זרה from the ו, and the community's other מצוות from 'מעיני'.

phrases.english: He derives it from "from the eyes" and "from the eyes."
phrases.notes: This is the same 'מעיני' link we saw back in step 8.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on 'מעיני' links the community's other מצוות to its עבודה זרה.

steps.title: What does רבי do with one law?
steps.stepSummary: רבי got the כרת rule from a different source, so the גמרא asks what he learns from 'תורה אחת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי, what does he do with this 'one law'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי and asks what he uses this פסוק for, since he does not need it for the כרת rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word of the Torah is supposed to teach something. Since רבי's source for the כרת rule is elsewhere, 'תורה אחת' needs a job of its own in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it?
One law

phrases.english: And Rabbi, this "one law",
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי, הַאי ״תּוֹרָה אַחַת״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the רבנן's source back on רבי and asks how he uses it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי learns from the פסוק 'תורה אחת'.

steps.title: רבי needs it for a teaching about individuals and the many
steps.stepSummary: רבי needs 'תורה אחת' for a ברייתא that starts by noting the Torah treats individuals and the many differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what was taught in a ברייתא: since we find that the Torah treated individuals and the many differently,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by quoting a ברייתא. This is only the start; the next step finishes the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא opens by noting that for עבודה זרה the Torah gives different laws to individuals and to the community. Where it goes from there will show what 'תורה אחת' teaches in רבי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it for
As taught in a ברייתא
Individuals
The many, the community

phrases.english: He needs it for that which was taught in a baraita:
Since we find
that the verse made a distinction between individuals and the many,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the answer to step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי uses 'תורה אחת' for a ברייתא about the difference between individuals and the many. The ברייתא continues past this point.

steps.title: The ברייתא finishes: different punishments, but the same offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא contrasts individuals (סקילה, money spared) with the many (סייף, money destroyed). Because of that difference one might split their קרבנות, so 'תורה אחת' teaches they are the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Individuals who serve idols are stoned, so their money is spared. The many are killed by the sword, so their money is lost. You might think we should also make their offerings different. That is why the verse says: 'One law shall be for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא that explains why רבי needs the words 'תורה אחת'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that the Torah really does treat the individual and the many differently, both in their death penalty and in their money. That difference could lead us to think their קרבנות also differ. 'תורה אחת' blocks that idea and says that for the קרבן they are treated the same.

keyTerms.meaning: Death by stoning, the more severe death penalty
Death by the sword, a lighter death penalty
Their money escapes, meaning it is spared and not destroyed
'One might think... so the verse teaches.' A standard way of raising a wrong idea and then using a פסוק to reject it

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי, 'תורה אחת' teaches that the individual and the many bring the same type of קרבן for עבודה זרה, even though their punishments differ.

phrases.english: Individuals are put to death by stoning
therefore their money is spared
The many are put to death by the sword
phrases.notes: 'The many' here means the people of a whole city that turned to idols, an עיר הנדחת.

phrases.english: therefore their money is lost
One might think we should make their offerings different too
So the verse teaches:
"One law shall be for you."
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:29

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that step 18 began quoting.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי uses 'תורה אחת' to teach that the קרבנות of the individual and the many are not different, even though their punishments are.

steps.title: רב חלקיה asks: without the פסוק, what else could they bring?
steps.stepSummary: רב חלקיה מהגרוניא points out that the ברייתא assumes we would have split the קרבנות without the פסוק. He asks what different קרבן would even have been possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חלקיה מהגרוניא challenges this. The reason is only because the Merciful One wrote 'One law shall be for you.' So without it, I would have said we should make them different. But what would they have brought?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חלקיה starts an attack on the ברייתא's need for the פסוק. This step sets up the question, and the next step goes through the options one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא implies that without 'תורה אחת' we would have given the many and the individual different קרבנות. רב חלקיה says that assumption only makes sense if some other קרבן was possible. So he asks what that other קרבן could be.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenges it strongly
'The reason is... so without this...' The גמרא is reading out what follows from the wording
I would have thought (the wrong idea we would have had)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳

phrases.english: Rav Chilkiya from Hagronya challenges this:
The reason is that the Merciful One wrote
"One law shall be for you"
but if not for this,
I would have said we should make them different.
What would they bring?
phrases.notes: He means the many who served idols. What different קרבן could they possibly bring?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא quoted in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that 'תורה אחת' is needed to stop us from giving the individual and the many different קרבנות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If no other קרבן was even possible, we never would have split them, so the פסוק teaches nothing.

steps.title: Every possible offering is already taken
steps.stepSummary: רב חלקיה goes through each animal. A פר, כשבה, שעיר, and a פר with a שעיר each already belong to another case. A שעירה is the individual's own קרבן, so no different option exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should they bring a bull? That is what the community brings for the other מצוות. A ewe? That is what an individual brings for the other מצוות. A male goat? That is what a נשיא brings for the other מצוות. A bull as a burnt-offering and a goat as a sin-offering? That is what the community brings for idolatry. So what else? A female goat? That is the individual's offering too!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חלקיה proves his challenge by checking every possible קרבן and showing that each one is already assigned to someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each animal is already the set קרבן for a different case. The Torah would not give the many who served idols a קרבן that duplicates another case's. The only option left is a שעירה, and that is exactly the individual's קרבן, so the many and the individual would end up the same anyway. That means 'תורה אחת' seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: A bull
A female sheep (a ewe), an individual's regular חטאת
A male goat, the חטאת of a נשיא
A female goat, the individual's חטאת for עבודה זרה
The leader or king of the Jewish people

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two goats. A שָׂעִיר (male) is the נשיא's קרבן, and a שְׂעִירָה (female) is the individual's. That one-letter difference is the whole key to the last line.
steps.whyThisMatters: This attack leaves the ברייתא's use of 'תורה אחת' looking unnecessary, so the גמרא will need to explain what the פסוק really adds.

phrases.english: Should they bring a bull?
That is what a community brings for the other מצוות.
A ewe?
That is what an individual brings for the other מצוות.
A male goat?
That is what a Nasi brings for the other מצוות.
A bull as a burnt-offering and a goat as a sin-offering?
That is what a community brings for idolatry.
So what else is left?
A female goat?
That is the individual's offering too!

steps.triggerLanguage: לַיְיתוֹ פַּר צִבּוּר בִּשְׁאָר מִצְוֹת הוּא דְּמַיְיתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the question 'מאי לייתו' from step 20 by ruling out every option.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for 'תורה אחת' in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each candidate animal already belongs to another case. The only one left, a שעירה, is the individual's own קרבן, so no split was ever possible and the פסוק seems unnecessary.

steps.title: We might have reversed the animals of the צבור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is needed. Since a צבור that sins through a הוראה of בית דין brings a פר for an עולה and a שעיר for a חטאת, we might have thought the many who sinned on their own bring the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed. You might have thought: since a community that sins because of the court's ruling brings a bull for a burnt-offering and a goat for a sin-offering, these people should also bring the opposite.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב חלקיה. There really was another option: the same two animals the צבור brings, but with their jobs switched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חלקיה said every animal already belongs to some other case. The answer is that 'different' does not have to mean a new animal. It can mean a known pair (פר and שעיר) with the roles flipped, a פר for the חטאת and a שעיר for the עולה. 'תורה אחת' rules that out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed (the פסוק is not extra)
You might have thought; it would have entered your mind to say
A ruling of בית דין, here one that wrongly allowed a sin
A burnt-offering, burned completely on the מזבח
The opposite, reversed

phrases.english: It is needed,
since you might have said:
since a community that sinned through the court's ruling
brings a bull as a burnt-offering
and a goat as a sin-offering,
these too should bring the opposite.
phrases.notes: 'These' are the many who sinned on their own, without the court. 'The opposite' means a bull for the sin-offering and a goat for the burnt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חלקיה's challenge from steps 20-21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a real alternative that the פסוק must exclude
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The many who sinned on their own would bring a פר for a חטאת and a שעיר for an עולה, the reverse of the צבור that sinned through a הוראה
steps.terutzMaskana: 'תורה אחת' teaches that the many bring the same קרבן as an individual

steps.title: Or: they need a different קרבן but have none
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: we might have thought the many need a different קרבן from an individual's, but the Torah never names one, so they would be left with no atonement at all. The פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: they need a different offering and have no way to fix it. The פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to רב חלקיה. This one accepts that no other animal was available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא agrees that no other קרבן fits. But that could have led to a worse conclusion: the many need a separate קרבן, none exists, so they simply cannot gain atonement. 'תורה אחת' tells us they bring the individual's קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively; another answer
A remedy, a way to fix the situation
It teaches us (the point the source is coming to make)

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers for why 'תורה אחת' is needed: (1) we might have reversed the פר and שעיר; (2) we might have thought the many have no קרבן at all. Either way, the פסוק teaches the many bring the same קרבן as an individual.

phrases.english: Alternatively,
they need a different offering and have no remedy
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, צָרִיךְ וְאֵין לוֹ תַּקָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the same challenge as step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframes the possible mistake as 'no קרבן at all' rather than 'a different קרבן'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The many need a separate קרבן but none exists, so they cannot gain atonement
steps.terutzMaskana: 'תורה אחת' gives them the individual's קרבן

steps.title: לוי asks why the משנה says fifteen and not sixteen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now turns back to the משנה. לוי asks רבי why the משנה lists fifteen women who exempt their צרות, when it could have listed sixteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי said to רבי: Why does the משנה teach fifteen? Let it teach sixteen!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the קרבנות discussion and goes back to the opening line of the משנה. לוי challenges the number fifteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה begins 'fifteen women exempt their צרות.' לוי thinks there is one more case that fits the rule, so the count should be sixteen. The extra case is not stated yet; the גמרא will spell it out.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this?
Let him teach (it should have said)

phrases.english: לוי said to רבי:
Why does he specifically teach fifteen?
phrases.notes: This is the first line of the משנה: fifteen women exempt their צרות from חליצה and יבום.

phrases.english: Let him teach sixteen!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: back to the number in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's count of fifteen women
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There seems to be a sixteenth case of an ערוה whose צרה is exempt, so the count is too low

steps.title: רבי's sharp response
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers that it seems לוי has no brain in his head, meaning the question has no basis.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It seems to me that he has no brain in his head.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי rejects לוי's question strongly before explaining why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only rejects the question. It does not yet explain the mistake. The next lines show what לוי was thinking and why it does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: It seems to me
A brain in his head

steps.confusionAlert: רבי speaks about לוי in third person ('he has no brain'), even though he is answering him directly.

phrases.english: He said to him:
It seems to me
that he has no brain in his head.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּמְדוּמֶּה לִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מוֹחַ בְּקׇדְקֳדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects לוי's challenge
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggestion of a sixteenth case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not stated yet; the explanation follows

steps.title: What did לוי have in mind? His mother raped by his father
steps.stepSummary: רבי spells out לוי's idea: the sixteenth case would be a man's mother who was raped by his father and later married his paternal brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are you thinking? His mother who was raped by his father?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבי names the case לוי was thinking of, so that the גמרא can next explain why it does not belong in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a man's mother cannot fall to him for יבום. But if she was only raped by his father and never married to him, she could later marry the father's other son. If that husband dies without children, she falls to her own son for יבום. That is לוי's sixteenth case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is your thinking?
A woman raped by his father (not married to him)
His mother

phrases.english: What is your thinking?
His mother who was raped by his father?
phrases.notes: Since she was never married to his father, she could later marry his father's other son, his half-brother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the reasoning behind רבי's rejection

steps.title: The sixteenth case is in dispute, so the משנה leaves it out
steps.stepSummary: רבי explains that the case of 'his mother raped by his father' is argued about by רבי יהודה and the רבנן, and our משנה does not list disputed cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case of his mother who was raped by his father is a dispute between רבי יהודה and the רבנן, and the משנה does not deal with disputed cases.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי finishes his answer to לוי. He explains why the sixteenth case was left out: it is not agreed on by everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, a woman raped by one's father is forbidden to the father's sons. So she could never be married to his brother, and the case would never come up. Since the case only works according to the רבנן, the תנא leaves it out, because he only lists cases that everyone agrees on.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman his father raped (not married to the father)
A dispute between opinions
רבי יהודה and the majority of Sages
It does not deal with (this kind of case)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a rule about how the משנה was written: it lists only agreed cases. The rest of this section tests that rule.

phrases.english: His mother who was raped by his father:
phrases.notes: This is the sixteenth case לוי wanted to add, the one spelled out in step 26.

phrases.english: is a dispute between רבי יהודה and the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה holds that a woman raped by your father is forbidden to you, so she could not marry the brother in the first place.

phrases.english: and [the משנה] does not deal with disputed cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבָּנַן הִיא, וּבִפְלוּגְתָּא לָא קָא מַיְירֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי's answer to לוי after spelling out לוי's proposed case in step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sixteenth case is in dispute, and the משנה lists only cases that everyone agrees on.

steps.title: But the משנה does include איסור מצוה and איסור קדושה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי's rule: the משנה does teach איסור מצוה and איסור קדושה, even though רבי עקיבא and the רבנן argue about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it really not deal with disputes? But there are איסור מצוה and איסור קדושה, which רבי עקיבא and the רבנן argue about, and the משנה teaches them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule that the תנא never includes disputed cases. It points to cases the משנה does teach that are in dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איסור מצוה (a woman forbidden by the Sages) and איסור קדושה (a woman forbidden by a regular prohibition) appear in a משנה. רבי עקיבא and the רבנן argue whether such women are fully exempt from יבום and חליצה. So the תנא clearly does teach disputed cases.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman forbidden by a rule of the Sages
A woman forbidden by a regular prohibition of holiness (not an ערוה)
And yet it is taught (in the משנה)

phrases.english: And does it not [deal with disputes]?
But there are the cases of a prohibition of מצוה and a prohibition of holiness,
which רבי עקיבא and the Rabbis argue about,
and they are taught!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule just stated in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the תנא does not include disputed cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה does teach איסור מצוה and איסור קדושה, which are in dispute between רבי עקיבא and the רבנן.

steps.title: The rule only applies to our chapter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the rule about leaving out disputes applies only to our chapter.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are speaking about our chapter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the rule so the challenge no longer works. Only this chapter avoids disputed cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cases of איסור מצוה and איסור קדושה are taught in a different chapter, not ours. So they do not break the rule, which was only about how our chapter was written.

keyTerms.meaning: In our chapter
We are saying (this rule)

phrases.english: We are speaking about our chapter.
phrases.notes: He means: the cases of רבי עקיבא are in a different chapter, so they don't count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule covers the whole משנה, so the cases of רבי עקיבא contradict it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule covers only our chapter, and those cases are in another chapter.

steps.title: But our chapter has the dispute of בית שמאי and בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: even in our chapter there is a dispute, since בית שמאי permit the צרות to the brothers and בית הלל forbid them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in our chapter it says that בית שמאי permit the rival wives to the brothers and בית הלל forbid them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the narrowed rule from step 29. It shows a dispute that is taught right in our chapter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our chapter teaches the famous argument about צרות: בית שמאי permit them to the brothers, and בית הלל forbid them. So even our chapter includes disputed cases, and the answer of step 29 seems not to work.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of שמאי
The school of הלל
Rival wives (other wives of the same husband)
They permit
They forbid

phrases.english: But [in our chapter] בית שמאי
permit the rival wives to the brothers,
and בית הלל forbid [them]!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי מַתִּירִין אֶת הַצָּרוֹת לָאַחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that our chapter does not include disputed cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our chapter teaches the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל about צרות.

steps.title: בית שמאי's view against בית הלל does not count as a real dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 30: a view of בית שמאי that argues against בית הלל is treated as if it were not in the משנה at all, so it does not make the case 'disputed.'
steps.simpleTranslation: When בית שמאי disagree with בית הלל, the opinion of בית שמאי is not considered part of the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי's rule. The argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל about the צרות is not a real dispute, because בית שמאי's opinion does not count when it goes against בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 30 said our chapter does contain a dispute, since בית שמאי permit the צרות and בית הלל forbid them. The answer is that everyone knows the הלכה does not follow בית שמאי against בית הלל, so their view is treated as if it were missing. That means the case of the צרות counts as undisputed, and רבי's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The students of שמאי, who often argue with בית הלל
The students of הלל, whose view is followed in practice
Literally 'in the place of'; here it means 'when arguing against'
It is not counted as part of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the words of בית שמאי are missing from the printed משנה. They are written there. The point is only that their view does not count as a real opinion when it goes against בית הלל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule found across the תלמוד: when בית שמאי argue against בית הלל, their view is set aside and the הלכה follows בית הלל.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai where they argue against Beit Hillel
phrases.notes: This goes back to the case from step 30, where בית שמאי permit the צרות to the brothers.

phrases.english: is not considered part of the Mishna.
phrases.notes: He means their view is treated as if it were not there, so it does not create a real dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: בית שמאי במקום בית הלל אינה משנה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 30 by taking away the value of בית שמאי's opposing view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Takes away the force of the counter-example: the opposing view does not count as a real opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument of בית שמאי and בית הלל about the צרות shows that our chapter does list disputed cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since בית שמאי's view against בית הלל is treated as if it were not in the משנה, the case of the צרות counts as undisputed, and רבי's rule holds.

steps.title: A new challenge from the brother who was never alive with his brother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises another case from our chapter that seems to be disputed: the wife of a brother who was never alive at the same time as the יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the case of the wife of his brother who did not live in the world together with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי's rule again with a new case from our chapter: a brother's wife where the brothers were never alive at the same time. This line sets up the case, and the גמרא will go on to show why it seems to be a dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer about בית שמאי only removed one example. Now the גמרא points to a different case in our chapter, אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו. The claim is that this case is also argued about, so our chapter would still contain a real dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But there is…', used to bring a counter-example
The wife of a brother who was not alive at the same time as the יבם, because the יבם was born after the first brother died

with whom he did not live in the world at the same time,

steps.triggerLanguage: והרי אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the answer about בית שמאי in step 31, the גמרא brings a new counter-example against רבי's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's rule from steps 27 and 29 that our chapter does not list disputed cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case of אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו is listed in our chapter, and the גמרא is about to show that it is disputed. That would mean our chapter does list a disputed case.
